feedback_prompts: Zero seats launched. Opened launch-authorized (session ses_613562a166235f0bfd33df89b96a65cb), compiled four bound seats, and the mandatory host hook refused both alignment-audit launches with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: host_workflow_turn_bindings.attempt_id'. The hook was correct; the defect is structural.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a hard architectural dead end: compile_bound_launch_plan generates attempt_id as f'attempt-{group_id}-{seat_index}-0' (dispatch_workflow.py:143), with no dispatch_id and no uniqueness source. The host_workflow_turn_bindings table enforces UNIQUE on attempt_id GLOBALLY, not scoped per dispatch. Meanwhile the appender FORCES every brownfield code dispatch to use exactly the canonical group ids alignment-audits, implementation and verification. Therefore every brownfield code dispatch in this repository produces the identical four attempt_ids, the first one consumes them permanently, and no second brownfield code dispatch can ever launch. The first attempt (2026-08-03-swu-aci-host-bus-integrity-001-code) consumed attempt-alignment-audits-0-0 and attempt-alignment-audits-1-0 on 2026-08-03.

WHY THIS WAS NEVER HIT BEFORE: every prior dispatch in this database used distinct, work-specific group ids (transformation-worker, topology-worker, divergence-designer, pdf-auditor, ...), so the unscoped attempt_id never collided. The canonical fixed group ids required for dispatch_type code are the first case where two dispatches must reuse the same group names, which is exactly where the missing scoping becomes fatal.

BOOTSTRAP DEADLOCK: the fix is to namespace attempt_id by dispatch_id in dispatch_workflow.py. That file is pinned in the Stage-E source manifest and is runtime source, so changing it under governance requires a code dispatch, and no further code dispatch can launch until it is changed. The deadlock cannot be broken from inside the governed code path.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME ATTEMPT, independent of the first: orchestration_bridge.py:293 passes the literal constant idempotency_key='bridge-session' to ensure_session, while the command digest covers an intent that includes the session name, and the aggregate is derived from origin_digest. Consequently, for a given --origin-ref, only ONE --session-name can ever be accepted; every later open with a different name raises IdempotencyConflict 'idempotency key reused with different digest'. This dispatch only opened at all because it was given the full 40-character commit SHA as origin-ref instead of the short SHA used by the previous attempt, which produced a different aggregate. That workaround is accidental, not designed.

THIRD DEFECT, from the previous attempt and still unfixed: service.py:5489 compares spawned prompt bodies to the ledger row's initial_prompt by exact string equality, while the parent must retype every prompt in its own text output because nothing in the runtime spawns seats. That relay is not byte-safe for non-ASCII, so every governed seat prompt must be pure ASCII, and nothing enforces or documents this.

COMMON SHAPE across all three, and across the two findings recorded earlier today: the enforcing half of each mechanism is built and the emitting or scoping half is not. A host hook accepts turn_ordinal > 0 with no emitter. A readiness-receipt schema has a strict validator and no producer. A capability_profile declares filesystem task-scoped-write with no enforcement. Prompt equality is checked byte-exactly over a channel that is not byte-safe. attempt_id is enforced unique over a generator that cannot produce unique values. Session idempotency is enforced over a key that is constant.

NOTHING WAS LEFT BEHIND: the hook blocked before any subagent started. No agent ran, no artifact was produced, and no file outside the compiled workflow inputs was touched. The hook fired correctly on both launch attempts.

F4, F5 and F6 remain unimplemented. Their implementation is fully specified by the two audits of the first attempt, preserved in that dispatch's close record, and the revised eight-path write_scope including local_pilot.py stands as correct.
